news.title: Infantino breaks cover to arrive for crisis talks after World Cup plot failed
news.lede: DISGRACED Fifa president Gianni Infantino has broken cover to attend an emergency meeting in Morocco. A Mercedes containing the beleaguered supremo was seen swooping into Fifa’s African base in Rabat. It’s the first time Infantino has been spotted since his disgraceful plot to sell a stake in Fifa tournaments including the World Cup came to light. The usually attention-seeking honcho is facing total crisis, with the Fifa chief losing support by the day.

news.title: The Club World Cup deals the knockout blow to Infantino
news.lede: Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football's governing body (UEFA), and Nasser Al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association, are holding an anticipated meeting in the city of Salzburg. Tension is rising between their organisations and world football's governing body (FIFA), specifically against its president Gianni Infantino. According to the "talkSPORT" network, the root of that tension lies in the possibility of the European clubs withdrawing from the 2029 Club World Cup, following UEFA's decision regarding the national teams in relation to the World Cup. Spanish newspaper "AS" reported that there is as yet no agreement between the European Club Association and FIFA to stage the 2029 Club World Cup, which makes talk of boycotting the tournament inaccurate for now.

news.title: Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request
news.lede: Jamie Carragher turned down FIFA 's request to publicly support the idea of holding the World Cup every two years rather than the traditional four, following a secret meeting. The Sky Sports pundit revealed he had spoken with former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, now FIFA's chief of global football development, as well as a number of ex‑players about the proposed overhaul. This summer's tournament was staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, with European champions Spain lifting the trophy for the first time in 16 years. Luis de la Fuente's side beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal.

news.title: Wenger breaks silence on Infantino's World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA’s chief of global football development Arsene Wenger says Gianni Infantino’s decision to withdraw from a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. Former Arsenal manager Wenger issued a statement on Tuesday morning a week on from the first reports emerging about Infantino’s plan to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and sell a 20 per cent stake in it to private equity.

news.title: Key questions as Infantino faces Fifa executives
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino will meet with senior leaders of football's world governing body on Wednesday as criticism of his now scrapped plan to sell off Fifa's commercial and event operations intensifies. After secretary general Mattias Grafstrom sent a highly critical internal memo to Fifa staff, Infantino summoned members of the Fifa management board to Morocco. Tuesday also saw chief of global football development Arsene Wenger insist he was "not involved" in Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, adding that aborting it was "absolutely necessary and beyond question".
